checks.result: 17 tests passed: real session bootstrap, membership/provisioning, tenant switching, delayed media, dirty editor, MFA/device approval, cookie refresh, Web Locks, cross-tab logout. These do not exercise Quote to Design to Production.

checks.result: pilot-gate.sh with PILOT_GATE_FOUNDATION_A=1 and explicit isolated database completed PASS. Log search returned no SKIP/skipped lines. Includes runtime-role RLS and pilot readiness. This is the component proof, not a rerun of the entire foundation-gate-a.sh wrapper.

checks.title: Baseline CI and local build
checks.result: Seven remote checks success on exact audited SHA, including Foundation Gate A. Local init, generated OpenAPI check, Web production build and deployment structural smoke passed. Structural smoke is not a deployed environment or restore rehearsal.

findings.title: Proyectar canvas collapses on mobile and tablet
findings.currentBehavior: At 390x844 and 768x1024 the rendered canvas has height zero. The furniture list and inspector remain visible but the design canvas disappears. At desktop 1280x720 it renders.
findings.expectedBehavior: A usable scene remains available at supported device sizes, or an explicit unsupported-device state explains the limitation.
findings.problem: Responsive design removes the primary work surface.
findings.businessImpact: A tablet demonstration cannot show the design workflow reliably.
findings.demoImpact: Blocker only if the planned demo uses these viewport sizes. Rehearsed desktop is a scoped workaround.
findings.technicalImpact: Responsive layout sizing fails for the canvas. Exact CSS root cause still needs a focused fix/retest.
findings.recommendation: PROPOSED: give the scene an explicit responsive minimum block size and verify list/scene/inspector composition. Until fixed, use a rehearsed desktop demo and disclose design-device limits.

findings.title: Default demo framing obscures the kitchen
findings.currentBehavior: The accepted Cocina López seed opens Proyectar with a large foreground wall hiding most furniture in the initial three-quarter view. Ocultar muros can be pressed but the captured view still has a major obstruction. Planta camera works and changes the scene.
findings.expectedBehavior: The first demo view makes the furniture composition understandable without recovery steps.
findings.problem: Initial impression is dominated by a wall rather than the product design.
findings.businessImpact: Reduces clarity and perceived product quality in the first design demonstration.
findings.demoImpact: Preselect and rehearse a clear camera; do not improvise the default view.
findings.technicalImpact: Camera/occlusion behavior needs targeted verification; no claim that all controls fail.
findings.recommendation: PROPOSED: define and test a clear initial camera for the canonical demo scene. Keep functional camera controls and verify occlusion by screenshot.
dependencies: Canonical demo seed and camera rehearsal
